prompt_en: Create a photographic sports image of a woman athlete in the middle of athletic movement. Use the supplied portrait as facial and hairstyle guidance, retaining the softly tapered face, dark expressive eyes, short dark bob and fine loose fringe as visible reference cues. She is practicing figure skating at an indoor ice rink, coming out of a broad curve toward the open ice. Her supporting skate runs along the curved track with the knee softly bent, her other leg trails clear of the surface, and her arms open away from her body to steady the glide. Her eyes follow the space ahead rather than the camera; her slightly parted lips and alert expression carry the effort of keeping the line. A simple deep-blue practice dress moves lightly at the hem above pale tights and white figure skates. At the supporting skate, a distinct white boot sole and raised heel sit above a visible metal mount; that mount links the sole and heel to a single narrow steel runner, whose lower edge meets the ice while the boot sole stays elevated. Give this supporting skate a clear side-biased profile, with the dark gap between sole and runner readable against pale ice. The photograph catches the instant when a tight turn releases into a longer, calmer glide: the fresh arc behind her and a few lifted ice grains give the movement a visible origin, while the wide clear ice ahead gives it somewhere to continue. Frame her whole body and both skates with breathing room beneath the blades and ahead of the direction of travel. Photograph from beside the rink at about waist height, in a gently frontal three-quarter view that lets her face, free leg, and supporting blade read separately. Cool rink light gives the ice a pale sheen and puts a quiet highlight along her hair, with natural facial texture and soft color in the cheeks. The rink boards and distant seating recede softly behind the crisp athlete and curved ice trace. Her poised presence is inviting but the athletic action remains the main attraction. Aim for the restrained intimacy of a practice photograph: an accomplished movement still requiring full attention, seen close enough to feel her concentration and wide enough to understand its balance.
